title: Your Group-Relative Advantage Is Biased
claim: Group-relative advantage estimates are systematically biased by prompt difficulty, and correcting this bias improves results across benchmarks and difficulty levels.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: radial bar chart, pie-chart comparison, radar chart
description: Three-panel figure. Panel (a) is a radial bar chart. Bars radiate from the center toward five benchmarks: OlympiadBench, MATH500, AIME25, AMC23 and Minerva. Each benchmark has paired bars for GRPO, GSPO and DAPO, with and without HA-DW. The HA-DW variants are hatched, and the colors are pink, olive and blue. Panel (b) uses 3D pie charts. Rows are a hard prompt and an easy prompt, and columns are rollout = 8 and rollout = 128. Yellow marks incorrect responses and light blue marks correct ones. Counts such as 1/7 and 9/119 are shown. Red arrows mark advantage overestimation, and boxes below give advantage values such as +2.65 and -0.38. Panel (c) is a radar chart over Easy, Mid and Hard difficulty. It compares GRPO (dashed blue) with GRPO+HA-DW (orange) and labels the percentage gains.
caption: (a) Comparison of the performance of RL algorithms with and without HA-DW on Qwen3-4B-Base across five mathematical reasoning benchmarks. (b) Significant biased advantage estimation on the MATH dataset under 8 and 128 rollouts. (c) Performance gain by GRPO+HA-DW on MATH500 stratified by difficulty levels.
abstract: Reinforcement Learning from Verifier Rewards (RLVR) has emerged as a widely used approach for post-training large language models on reasoning tasks, with group-based methods such as GRPO and its variants gaining broad adoption. These methods rely on group-relative advantage estimation to avoid learned critics, yet its theoretical properties remain poorly understood. In this work, we characterize conditional estimation bias in group-relative advantages among non-degenerate groups. For mean-centered advantages under binary rewards, our analysis shows negative conditional mean estimation errors for hard prompts and positive errors for easy prompts. At the response level, correct answers to hard prompts are underweighted, while incorrect answers to easy prompts receive insufficient penalties. To address this issue, we propose History-Aware Adaptive Difficulty Weighting (HA-DW), an adaptive reweighting scheme that adjusts advantage estimates based on an evolving difficulty anchor and training dynamics. Both theoretical analysis and experiments on five mathematical reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that HA-DW consistently improves performance when integrated into GRPO and its variants. Our results suggest that correcting biased advantage estimation is critical for robust and efficient RLVR training.
